closest_known_result.statement: Van Assche constructs Padé approximants from little-q-Legendre polynomials and proves irrationality results in his stated setting. The present route fixes p=3/2, evaluates the same family at all outward exponents m>=n, charges the necessary cyclotomic and homogeneous denominator clearing, and combines that cost with the source's positive error bounds.
closest_known_result.exact_delta: The authored conclusion is not a new Padé approximation theorem: it is the forced-clearing main term (n*m+n^2/2)log(4/3)+(3/pi^2)m^2 log 3>0 before primitive common-content division, plus the all-index restriction that content coprime to the clearing value divides 3^n+2^n.

disconfirming_evidence.finding: The claim that every remaining content prime has order at most 2n is false, with exact witnesses including (n,m,ell,ord)=(8,64,59,58).
disconfirming_evidence.effect: A simple bounded-order proof cannot eliminate clearing-supported primitive content; the residual cannot be dismissed as a formal nuisance.

disconfirming_evidence.finding: The Lean statements check finite-scale source-balance identities and positivity, not Van Assche's asymptotics or an all-index primitive-content bound.
disconfirming_evidence.effect: The all-outward conclusion is source-backed ordinary mathematics with formal local arithmetic components, not a fully Lean-checked scalar impossibility theorem.

disconfirming_evidence.finding: Van Assche's paper is the stated 2001 little-q-Legendre/Lambert-series Padé source; its metadata and abstract establish the surrounding construction but do not state the present rational-base 3/2 claim.
disconfirming_evidence.effect: Attribute the analytic family to Van Assche and retain the local calculation as a distinct, no-priority synthesis.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: For the source little-q-Legendre family at p=3/2, every outward scalar evaluation m>=n has a positive forced-clearing main term before primitive common-content division. The part of that common content coprime to the clearing value is confined by the adjacent determinant to a divisor of 3^n+2^n; clearing-supported content remains open.
forbidden_wording: All scalar Padé constructions at 3/2 are impossible.
Van Assche's paper proves the 3/2 obstruction.
The Lean source proves Van Assche asymptotics or all-index content control.
claim_boundary.open_boundary: A quantitative all-index bound on primitive common content supported on the clearing factors, strictly below the positive main term, would close this scalar family; an explicit quadratic-content construction would refute the obstruction's remaining hope. Higher-rank and inward-evaluation architectures are not covered.
